new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbum (Nganha) is a two-level (H/L) tone language; none of the accessible sources says anything about word stress or accent. The primary phonology (Hagège 1968; 1970, with a prosody/tone chapter) could not be opened beyond a segmental excerpt.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements only (lexical tone classes on verbs, H-L melodies on words); no stress domain described. Boyd's statement is family-level (Southern Mbum group = Mbum, Mbere, Kpere) reported second-hand by Elders.
new_statements.identity_note: All modern sources (Hagège 1968/1970, Mohamadou 2006, Kunzmann 2026, Beyer 2024) describe the Mbum of Nganha (central Adamawa plateau, near Ngaoundéré), the prestige variety of mbum1254; Hino 1978 is Mbang-Mboum (same central group). Kouemou Mouga 2001 describes Gbete/Kepere (eastern variety, Bertoua-Belabo), also under mbum1254. Boyd's 'Southern Mbum group' statement covers Mbum together with Mbere and Kpere. Not to be confused with Karang (kara1481) or Nzakambay (nzak1247; Ladogana 1991 'Grammaire mbum nzaka mbay').
